mission: Desh stops speaking like an analyst and starts speaking like someone who cares whether Ben survives this pattern, while Sera's certainty visibly falters at the edge of the room.
why_now: The Jacen recognition has to be met with a sentence from someone who was there. Desh is the only person on the ship who can speak this one, and the scene earns his arc-moment-of-truth. Sera's fissure cannot land without the preceding Ch 17 s2 silence; it also cannot wait past Ch 18 because the Ch 19 scenes require her to be someone who has already begun to doubt. Two threads, one scene, rendered through the same physical space.
conflict: The assessment Ben needs is the assessment he does not want. Desh delivers it as professional debrief until the last sentence, which he delivers as himself. Ben cannot argue with any part of it. At the same time, Sera enters the edge of the cockpit, registers Desh's last sentence, starts to speak — and does not. The line she would have said in Ch 14 is now a line she cannot say. The cost of the not-saying is held in her hand on the frame.
turning_point: Desh lands the personal line — the 'another good person' echo that hits Ben as Jacen, Torin, and himself simultaneously. Desh does not have to specify. In the same beat, Sera at the cockpit frame — hand paused, breath held, the sentence not emerging. Two turning points in one frame.
opening_hook: Desh doesn't frame it as a warning. He frames it as a debrief. 'Let me walk you through the team status.' It's the most frightening sentence Ben has heard on this trip.
closing_hook: Desh's final assessment names the leadership shift Ben has to make — the group needs a reason to stay that is not Ben telling them to. Ben doesn't have that reason yet. But he knows where to look — somewhere in the Codex notes he bookmarked and hasn't revisited. At the cockpit doorway, Sera's hand is still on the frame. She walks away without the sentence. Ben watches her go
emotional_trajectory: Professional assessment -> personal investment revealed -> the challenge to Ben's leadership approach -> Sera's unsaid line held in the air

stakes.personal: Desh's arc turning — obligation becoming investment; Ben receiving the Jacen echo from the only other witness
stakes.interpersonal: The group's survival as a functioning unit; Sera's defence-of-Torin instinct visibly faltering for the first time in the book
stakes.external: A fractured group cannot face Veraine at Veranthos; Sera's unarticulated cascade-acceleration intuition, planted here, will reach into the Ch 21 decision-space

setting: Aboard the Steady Returns — cockpit, night cycle
sensory_details: Instrument lights; Desh's voice steady and professional until the last line, when it is not; the nav display showing Veranthos's system approaching; the countdown timer Desh posted on the bulkhead, smaller every time Ben reads it; the specific quiet of Sera's arrival at the cockpit doorway; her weight shifting forward onto the ball of her front foot, then settling back; her hand finding the frame; the small intake of breath that is the beginning of a sentence; the breath releasing without the sentence; her footsteps moving away down the corridor, measured, not-quite-steady
canon_elements_needed: Jedi mission-debrief structure used as personal confrontation vehicle
Dantari philosophical discipline under internal doubt (Sera's posture)
action_beats: Desh pulls out his datapad and walks Ben through each team member's status — clinical, precise, devastating
Desh taps the countdown timer he posted on the bulkhead without looking at it
Sera arrives at the cockpit doorway as Desh lands the personal line; her hand finds the frame; her breath starts a sentence and does not release it
Desh delivers the personal line. Ben does not answer. Desh does not need him to
Sera walks away down the corridor without the sentence. Ben registers the absence. Neither Ben nor Desh remarks on it
Ben stares at the Codex file bookmark on his datapad after Desh leaves — the resonance note waiting
promises_planted: Sera's unarticulated cascade-acceleration intuition (plants Ch 18 s2, pays at Ch 21 when the forcible-disengagement cost becomes the decision-point)
The resonance-note emphasis waiting to shift (plants Ch 18 s2, pays at Ch 18 s3)
notes: Desh's line and Sera's unsaid line are the scene. Everything else should point at those two absences becoming visible.
